chunks: Ibn Muskan narrated from al-Hudhayl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who relies on the counting of his female companion in the tawaf, whether it suffices for both of them and for the child, he عليه السلام said: “Yes. Do you not see that you follow the Imam when you perform salat (prayer) behind him, and it is similar to that?”

key_terms.الطَّوَافِ: tawaf, the circumambulation around the Kaʿbah
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the prayer leader; here used in the analogy
key_terms.تَأْتَمُّ: you follow in prayer behind a leader
key_terms.عَدَدِ: the count or number of circuits
key_terms.يُجْزِيهِ: suffices or is valid for him

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to rely on someone else’s counting of the circuits during tawaf?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning reliance on another person’s counting during tawaf. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام permits it, drawing an analogy to following the Imam in congregational salat (prayer), which indicates acceptability in this ritual context.
